DOUBLE PROMOTION

In this issue of the Belgravian you will read of our promotion in both the British League and Southern Leagues. If all goes well we could make Division 1 of the BAL in our Centenary Year. It is definitely possible - if we get everyone's support next season.

items.heading: CHANGES AHEAD
items.summary: Editorial on the growing television and sponsorship money in athletics and the need for it to reach clubs, officials and grass-roots support.
items.text:
CHANGES AHEAD

While at grass roots level little seems to be changing in the athletics world, at International level the gradual march towards Semi-Professionalism goes on unabated. The money which will come into our sport in the years ahead will pose special problems for Clubs and it is far from clear how it will all end. Take for example the pulling power of Televised events. From 1985 onwards the AAA's and BAAB will receive over a 5 year period monies exceeding £13.5 million from TV and sponsorship deals. Somehow much of this must come through to the Clubs and the AAA's recognise that without the support of Clubs, their officials, organising expertise and not least of all the support of the athletes themselves the whole thing could go badly wrong.

The year ahead should see many points resolved and it is important that Belgrave has a view and a say in these important decisions. Whatever the outcome we must realise that our top athletes will be part of a world which we have not seen before. Let us hope that their hard work, dedication and talent will be fairly rewarded. Let us also hope that they will remember their roots and continue to support all those who have supported them in the past and who will continue to support them in the future.

items.heading: grapevine
items.summary: Grapevine club gossip column: Tom Carter's presidential year, a birth for the Biscoes, John Gladwin's club 1500m record and drug test, members leaving for US universities, Charlie Gillett's music career and other personal news, Andy North and Michael Blackmore, and a new Gleave on the way.
items.text:
grapevine

We were delighted to see President Tom Carter and Ethel at our British League home fixture in August. Ethel is making a rapid recovery following a stroke earlier in the year which required a brief period of hospitalisation. Although Tom must have found his Presidential year very demanding he has not missed any of our important meetings and visited members at Belgrave Hall at least 3 times per week.

Getting results and news items from Gordon Biscoe has not always proved the easiest of tasks for your Editor. Not surprising, therefore, that the Belgravian of last April contained no details of a forthcoming happy event for Margaret and Gordon. On August 31st at Epsom District Hospital, Richard Dennis Edward Biscoe weighed in at a healthy 5lb 15oz. Congratulations from your many friends at Belgrave.

Stuart Paton's Club 1500m record has been bettered several times this year by Stuart himself, Gary Staines and John Gladwin. When John finally reduced it to 3:39.47 at Meadowbank he also set another Belgrave first. Along with Steve Cram and Alan Wells, John was selected for drug testing. Training at the Belgrave Hall bar proved invaluable as John downed 7 lagers before obliging!!

Kevin Sturman and Paul Richley departed our shores mid-summer for life at U.S. Universities. Kevin has returned to South Ilinois while Paul has gone to Iowa State with his sparring partner from Windsor - Andrew Pettigrew.

Gordon Doubleday still visits us from Bath whenever possible. Gordon has recently been elected a Life Member of Somer A.C. and in September was re-elected President of "The Centurians" whose membership is confined to those walkers who have covered 100 miles in 24 hours.

Our Vet sprints record holder - Charlie Gillett's hidden talents surfaced in a recent edition of The Sunday Telegraph's Colour Supplement. To quote the summary of a revealing 3 page article 'He is one of rock music's unsung heroes; an authoritative writer and broadcaster, a sharp talent spotter (he championed Elvis Costello and Dire Straights). His book, "The sound of the City", published in 1970 and now revised and re-issued, was a classic in a field which then hardly existed.'

Funny how conversations with strangers often turn to running. A recent chat with a Leatherhead football club supporter revealed he had shared a bunkroom with Ted Stimpson in the 1940-41 war. 'Taffy' Jones sends his best wishes to Sargent Ted of 345 Heavy Anti Aircraft Battery - Royal Artillery. Taffy remembers "Ted was always dashing off somewhere to race a mile".

Honary Coaching member Mike Dunphy and wife Ann are moving house from Welwyn Garden City to High Wycombe. Mike who has coached many of our fine middle distance men will be cutting back on some of his coaching commitments. We wish them happiness in their new house.

Simon Williamson indicated to Bob Bridges that he would be unavailable for Southern League duties this summer. On being pressed he revealed that wedding bells in September were the reason. We wish the bride and groom good fortune.

Remember those promising Youths -Andy North and Michael Blackmore? We hear that Andy has been invited to Michael's wedding in January but as it clashes with the Surreys we will have to lay on some high speed transport if our top Junior is to make both events.

We also hear that there is another little Gleave on the way. Congrats and best wishes to Mum and Dad.

items.heading: MEMBERS HONOURED
items.summary: Report that the September AGM made Colin Pearson and Brian Gorman life members and elected Ernest Obeng, Harry Porter and Leo Coy Vice Presidents.
items.text:
MEMBERS HONOURED

At the September AGM, Colin Pearson and Brian Gorman were voted life members for services to the Club. Colin has been active over the last 10 years or so providing support to Gordon Biscoe in running the Road and Cross Country Section. Brian Gorman is widely known for initiating new members to the joys of training over Wimbledon common. In addition he has looked after teas and sandwiches at Belgrave Hall every Saturday afternoon for many years and lays on a special spread for visiting teams. Truly one of our backroom boys'

Unusually too we saw this year the election of 3 Vice Presidents at the AGM; Ernest Obeng for his services to the Club and for many years of International Standard performances, Harry Porter for his enormous work output as part of the small team building up our Ladies Section and Leo Coy who for 10 years has been responsible for compiling the U.K. 5000m, 1000m and 3000m S/C Rankings for NUTS. In addition Leo has been Results Secretary for the Southern League for the last 8 years and as joint team manager has played a major part in the building up of our 'A' track and field side which has gained promotion in each of the last 3 seasons.

We are fortunate in having men of this quality taking on greater responsibilities for the future.

items.heading: DINNER DANCE
items.summary: Report on the oversubscribed club Dinner/Dance at Bourne Hall, Ewell, organised by Bill Couzens and Brian Pritchard.
items.text:
DINNER DANCE

A new organising duo, a change of date plus a change of venue provided the backdrop for this years Dinner/Dance. It was with some trepidation therefore, that Bill Couzens and Brian Pritchard awaited the response as tickets went on sale. They need not have worried. By September the 175 places were over-subscribed with a waiting list for cancellations. So why such enthusiasm? Well the venue seemed a big attraction. Bourne Hall in Ewell provides extensive dining and separate dancing facilities in a village setting. Add to that music supplied by the popular 'Jaguars' and with the equally popular Ann and Bernie Ford as principal guests you have the formula for success.

Our younger members were well represented and it was perhaps inevitable that our 3 fastest 1500m men would be among the unofficial 'cabaret' provided by the middle distance team. The raffle must surely have lost money (although 'No!' says Bill) as the glittering prizes were topped by non-other than a colour television.

The evening proved a great success. Jenny and John Martin travelled all the way from Gloucestershire and Jenny's many Belgrave friends were delighted to see that she is now recovering from a period in hospital. Evelyn and Ted Stimpson were also official guests - a fitting honour in the year when Ted is honoured as President of the Middlesex AAA's. Congratulations then to Bill and Brian. We're already booking tickets for next year!

items.heading: COLD COMFORT
items.summary: Humorous note on John Rayner's triathlon in Leicester, where competitors changed in the open air after a cold quarry swim.
items.text:
COLD COMFORT

John Rayner recently completed a couple of Triathlon's. After the first stage of an event in Leicester - a half mile swim in a deep quarry - all competitors (male and female) discarded their wet costumes together in the open air in preparation for the bike stage. At this point, one lady competitor commented that she didn't think the chaps were up to much. Apparently this was not a reference to their efforts in the swim, but rather to other factors brought about by the cold water!

items.heading: JOE COLEMAN - PRESIDENT
items.summary: Profile of new club President Joe Coleman, a member since 1927, walker and Grade 1 judge, with a photo of the Walking Section congratulating him.
items.text:
JOE COLEMAN - PRESIDENT

Joe Coleman was elected a member on the 6th October 1927. From early days he was involved in all aspects of the Club and performed with distinction at Track and Field. In the mid thirty's he was scoring in our top Walking teams. He gained a first class standard in the 1938 AAA's Championships and won the coveted 'Fowler Dixon' style award. In 38 and 39 he was 3rd in our Open walk behind Harry Churcher. He achieved National 'fame' in 1939 when he and brother Len deadheated in the RWA National 10 mile Championship, and led Belgrave to a team win.

Like many top class athletes his career was interrupted by the 2nd World War but he came back to score again in many of our Walking teams. In 1952 Joe was elected a Vice President of Surrey CAAA for whom he had competed in the Inter County Championships in earlier years. His experience and knowledge was passed on to many young athletes when he became a Grade 1 Judge in the early 1950's. Since then Joe has enhanced the reputation of Belgrave in the Walking World as he has travelled the Country judging top class events.

A life time spent with the club and now the holder of its highest Office we can be certain that Belgravians will benefit from his vast experience and knowledge of the athletic world in the year ahead.

items.heading: From the President
items.summary: New President Joe Coleman's message thanking members for his election and calling for effort to revive the cross-country team and support the Ladies section.
items.text:
From the President

Fellow Belgravians,

Firstly, let me thank the council of P.P's who sorted me out for nomination and to the members at the A.G.M. who confirmed their nomination of me as the President of Belgrave Harriers for the coming year.

I value this office very much, and since joining the Club in 1927 I have had great pleasure in rubbing shoulders with many fine men as athletes, officials and supporters of our club.

We have enjoyed many successes, individually and teamwise in both running and walking sections of the club, and whilst the walkers have managed to maintain their winning ways, the X-Country men have not managed to match our pre-war and early post-war achievements not for the lack of endeavour but I do feel that if we made a real effort to harness our resources we could get the Bels singing again. The Track men have had some fine results likewise the younger age groups but Ladies section requires all the help and support we can give. The Roll of Presidents on the board at Belgrave Hall is an impressive one, and I will try to live up to the traditions that these men have set.

Here's to the coming year, let us make it one to remember. Good Luck and every success to all members and sections of the Club.

Joe Coleman.

items.heading: W.G. 'BILL' WEBB - 90 YEARS YOUNG
items.summary: Tribute to W.G. 'Bill' Webb on his 90th birthday, recalling his cross-country running for Belgrave from 1927, with a photo of him holding a decanter.
items.text:
W.G. 'BILL' WEBB - 90 YEARS YOUNG

On 9 August 1984 Bill Webb celebrated his 90th birthday. As he himself said, "There is nothing particularly meritorious in reaching 90, I just happened to be born with the right genes!" But he was also born with a charm which has endeared him to successive generations of Belgravians.

Bill Webb joined Belgrave in 1927, following a period of six years at Polytechnic Harriers and several traumatic wasted years in the first World War. At 33 years of age he was a mature newcomer who made his mark immediately by finishing 8th in the Yacht '3' that year with 15:55 (off 25 secs). In only his second match for Belgrave he closed-in our scoring team just behind first-team regulars Wally Bayliss and Micky Pyer. The Belgravian Scribe was induced to write "The runners have lately been joined by W.G.Webb and A.Robertshaw and I suggest that the presence of these valuable men gives our team a new impetus of enthusiasm."

Webb and Robertshaw were just the injection Belgrave needed and they celebrated by gaining bronze team medals in the South of Thames Senior of 1928 - our first medals in the event for 24 years! Bill went on to be our second scorer in the "Southern" and our first man home in the "National" at Leamington. A final flourish in the London-Brighton Relay and he had in one season established himself as a remarkably consistent runner who would always respond to the occasion. Within a year he was elected Captain.

Bill Webb's charming disposition concealed a very determined athlete, but it also revealed a willing Belgravian prepared to step into the shoes of W.H.Hare who had done so much to improve our finances. In 1943 he was elected Honorary Treasurer, a post he held for 14 years, the longest on record.

His service to the Club was first acknowledged in 1948 when he was elected President for two years. His 90th birthday was the occasion for fellow-Belgravians to make a further acknowledgement. At Belgrave Hall on Saturday 11 August a large gathering of members enjoyed a social evening in the company of Bill Webb who enraptured his audience with a lucid account of those early days. To mark the occasion our President, Tom Carter, presented him with a cut-glass decanter bearing a silver necklace engraved with the good wishes of the Club to which he has remained so loyal.

items.summary: Letter from Bill Webb to the President thanking fellow Belgravians for the gifts and gathering marking his 90th birthday.
items.text:
Dear Mr. President,

I am only now recovering from the series of events occasioned by my reaching the age of 90 on the 9th August, 1984. I was overwhelmed with kindness, congratulations and good wishes which helped to make my day a very happy one. None more so than those wishes sent by fellow Belgravians, and the more tangible symbol of those wishes which you so graciously presented to me, on their behalf, at the special social gathering at the Belgrave Hall. It was a memorable and most emotive evening to me, and one which will be inscribed indelibly in my memory.

Through you, Mr. President, I should like to express my humble and sincere thanks to all who so kindly and generously contributed to this most wonderful and truly Belgravian gesture.

I do not apologise for having reached this specific age. Belgrave is partly responsible. I came to the club at the relative old age of 38, following what had been a traumatic period of my life. The club accepted me, rehabilitated me and made me feel younger and younger. I was proud to play a small part in a wonderful team whose ultimate goal was to win the highest honours in the field of athletics, and to own their own headquarters. They achieved both.

I am happy to observe the quality and efficiency of our existing teams, to whom we all owe a debt of gratitude for the continuity of the Belgrave Tradition of "service to the club to the advantage of the whole". They will leave a bright light shining to guide their successors on their way.

Bidding continued success to the Club.

Sincerely,
W.G. (Bill) Webb

items.text:
MEMBERSHIP SECRETARY'S NOTES

The growth of the Club has been quite noticeable during the last few years. Obviously with the influx of marathons we have picked up members on this front, but having done their "one off" retire to oblivion and are eventually deleted from our records. Despite this we have breached the genuine 700 members mark and are now heading to 800.

I have, since taking over the job, requested efficiency in sending in subscriptions, change of address etc. but like most clubs, suffer from some who think reminders and requests do not apply to them.

With that in mind, I should like every member to consider himself or herself as a link in the chain and not just a pebble on the beach.

items.heading: OFFICIAL CHANGES
items.summary: Report on the club's new committee and sub-committee structure approved at an EGM, and the changes of officers at the September AGM, with profiles of retiring Hon. Gen. Sec. Derek Crookes and his successor Bill Laws, and of retiring Hon. Treasurer Jim Heathfield and his successor Ron Severn.
items.text:
OFFICIAL CHANGES

Structure

Our growing membership has resulted in greater activity in all sections and over the last few years it has become increasingly difficult to handle all Club business at monthly Committee meetings. Derek Crookes has been looking at ways of streamlining operations and his master plan was put to an EGM in the summer which approved the new arrangements. From now on the Committee will comprise of all Sectional Secretaries (or nominees) plus the Club's Trustees and 5 members elected at the AGM. Past Presidents may attend in a non-voting capacity and there will be many occasions when their specific past experiences and knowledge will be sought.

In parallel with this re-organisation a series of Sub-Committees will be set up based on separate Sectional activities and interests. These groups will be charged with promoting their Sections activities and will produce plans, targets and budgets. It is intended that as our finances move back into a healthier state following the Belgrave Hall re-development programme, each Section will be provided with its own monies following approval by the Committee of individual Section's targets and budget plans. In this way individual Sectional Secretaries and Team Managers will have greater freedom in day to day operations and financial matters. Naturally proper accounting will be required and at the end of each year results will be compared with targets. It will be up to each Section to argue its case and get the funding it needs.

We will need to feel our way into these new arrangements. New people are coming into the Management side. There will be difficulties but with our usual tolerance and understanding problems will be quickly ironed out and we can move to a simpler and more effective management system.

People

Each year at the September AGM we say farewell to the retiring President and welcome the new one. A hearty vote of thanks was given to Tom Carter for all his work during a year of office made particularly difficult by Ethel's illness. The meeting was particularly sad as both Derek Crookes and Jim Heathfield stepped down from office following terms of service spanning a period of time during which Belgrave's fortunes have seen a quite remarkable upturn.

HON. GEN. SEC.
Derek Crookes took over the post of Hon. Gen.Sec. in September 1978 and played an active and major part in the amalgamation plans. It was mainly Derek's efforts which resulted in the influx of the fine athletes and officials from Surrey A.C. who now play an important part in our expanding activities. During his 6 year period as Hon.Gen.Sec. Derek was elected President in 1981 and the following year served as joint President with Geoff Davis. In his final year of office he took the initiative in proposing and developing the re-organised Management Structure which has now come into operation. His services will not be lost completely as he has taken on the vacant post of Coaching Secretary. We can expect that there will soon be improvements to our Club Coaching arrangements once Derek has turned his full attention to the problems which currently exist. (For further details of Derek refer to the October 81 Belgravian).

Bill Laws takes over as Ho.Gen.Sec. on the promise that the new Organisational Structure will make the job less onerous. Bill joined Belgrave in 1952 while at Emanuel School. His membership lapsed when he moved North and he rejoined in 1963. He became a Committee member in 1974 and organised the Dinner/Dance for 5 years. His forte is looking after special projects. He negotiated the Sports Council Grants for the 1976 Hall improvement and the G.L.C. Grants for the latest Hall developments. In 1982 Bill spent quite a lot of time persuading the GLC to invest in putting the all weather track at our home track in Battersea Park. Bill gained a first in Mech. Engineering at Brunel University. He is a Chartered Engineer and is a Fellow of the Institute of Mechanical Engineers and a Fellow of the Institute of Energy. He was Project Manager for Belgrave on the latest Hall Development. In his spare time he has Edited the Belgravian since September 1979 and after producing the last 10 Editions is looking for someone else to ease into the job over the next year or so.

HON. TREASURER
Jim Heathfield took over the job of Hon. Treasurer in September 1979 and under his careful control funds soon grew to a level which permitted the recent Hall development project to proceed. Whereas most Club Officials perform duties different from their business activities, with Jim Belgrave work was very much an additional burden as he is an Accountant within the Ministry of Defence! With turnover now well into 5 figures keeping all the Accounts and cash flows under control, is practically a full time occupation, and it is much to Jim's credit that he managed to convey an air of complete calm during periods of difficulty. Unlike many Accountants, Jim was always anxious that our hard won savings should be put to work for the Club's future and his wholehearted support for our development projects has been an essential part of the success story. Sadly Jim is 'resting down' due to pressure of work but hopes to become involved again in the not to distant future. We thank him for all his efforts on our behalf.

Ron Severn has taken up the mantle of Hon. Treasurer and it would be difficult to find someone better qualified. A lawyer and Accountant by profession he has already made an impact in the short period he has been with Belgrave (see the April 84 Belgravian for a full C.V.!). Ron has been posing the sort of questions about our aims and aspirations which someone fresh to the scene can do. We welcome Ron to his first Belgrave Office and wish him good luck in the year ahead.

items.heading: BELGRAVE HALL DEVELOPMENT
items.summary: Report on the completed redevelopment of Belgrave Hall: the refurbished upstairs club room, remodelled changing rooms and busy new gymnasium, with thanks to the volunteers, the architect and donors to the Appeal Fund.
items.text:
BELGRAVE HALL DEVELOPMENT

Well, its finished! And everyone who visits Belgrave Hall is amazed at the transformation of our Headquarters. Upstairs we have created one of the finest club rooms you could wish to find. With; new windows faithfully repeating the original pattern, a £6000 maple floor lovingly sanded and polished by Harry Porter, new gas fired radiators plus velvet curtains and carpets in club colours, we have a most fitting setting for the Club Honours Boards. Add to this delicate colouring scheme to augment the soft furnishings and it is no wonder that Bill Couzens has been inundated with requests to hire the new facility. Already bookings from Art and Exercise classes are near capacity and our investment is beginning to show the cash returns which the Finance Committee was predicting two years ago.

Downstairs the mens changing facilities have been remodelled to give a slightly larger floor area following the removal of the old staircase. The interest in the new Gymnasium has been fantastic. Within three weeks of opening Mike Winch and Judy Oakes reported full capacity with opening on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays from 2 p.m. to 9 p.m. International athletes from as far afield as St. Albans make the trek to Belgrave Hall to obtain the benefit of the new facilities. Many of our members including nine of our British League team now train regularly in the Gymnasium with Mike and we look forward to big improvements in their 1985 performances. Interspersed with the specialist training sessions are strength and fitness classes for ladies and other members of the public. All this is again providing a big boost to our income.

Now that the operating patterns are getting sorted out following the inevitable teething problems, we can look forward to a good social calendar and hopefully you will come along and take advantage of your Club's facilities.

We are indeed fortunate that a major scheme of this nature can be planned, financed and progressed solely through the voluntary work so freely given by a few of our loyal members. Let us, therefore, through the pages of the Belgravian thank all who gave so much of their time and efforts and in particular; Ian Horton whose original conceptual designs formed the basis for the scheme as it has evolved, Tom Carter who has acted as Clerk of the Works making frequent site visits to check progress, Bill Couzens who has been responsible for specifying and procuring the various services, Bill Laws who was Project Manager and finally Harry Porter who has saved the Club so much money by putting the finishing touches to the Contractor's structural work.

We also owe a big debt of thanks to our Architect - David Lawton, R.I.B.A. who fulfilled the targets we set with great dedication and professionalism and at a fee especially reduced as his contribution to this worthwhile project.

And finally a big thank you to all those who have contributed to the Development by responding to our Appeal Fund. Over the two years to June 1984 donations totalled £1,496 but were swelled in September following a direct appeal by Past President Charlie Manning which added a further £1,085 to the funds for the Hall development.

Gordon Doubleday recently made a lightning trip from Bath to London to meet Edmund Donovan who is visiting London from the U.S.A. with wife Daye. Gordon writes -

"One of our oldest members, Edmund Donovan, O.B.E. was recently over here from New York where he lives. He was a Belgravian before the 1914-18 War, afterwards he went to the U.S.A. Unfortunately an accident to his hip has left him mostly confined to an invalid chair. His interest in the Club is undiminished and he always looks forward to reading the "Belgravian". He was accompanied by his charming wife Daye who originated from Fulham. Edmund is intensely proud of being a Belgravian and sings our praises in the U.S.A. He recalled C.C. runs from the "Spenser Arms" and the "Green Man" from former Club H.Q's and of course, Battersea Park. He sends his regards to all, particularly those who he knows."

items.heading: WALKING
items.summary: Carl Lawton's review of the walking section's year: a National 10 win and other team placings, Graham Seatter's Leicester Mercury win, British vests for Richard Dorman and Stephen Marshall, and the Ladies Section led by Rachel Parrott.
items.text:
WALKING

Casting ones thoughts back to the beginning of the year, we visualised having the strongest distance team for many years. But it did not materialize. We were unable to have our fittest teams out when needed and things did not work out. However, we did have partial success - the win in the National 10 was followed by 2nd in the 20kms and 2nd in the 35kms, but 7th in the 50kms with a team average age of 45 was not something to write home about. Regretably we ended up having to have only John Keown flying the flag for us in the Hastings and the Brighton which I fear is no credit to us by not being able to turn out teams. Maybe next year will be different.

Paul Warburton has returned to England after his 12 months in America and he hopefully replaces, in person, if not speed, Graham Seatter who has helped Belgrave to various placings during the year, and not forgetting his win in the Leicester Mercury in 2:26.56.

Congratulations to Richard Dorman and Stephen Marshall on gaining British Vests during the year. Regretably Stephen has had his year torn apart due to work commitments.

One must not forget that we have a Ladies Section and although not quite as prolific as the men we have been turning out teams and individuals at various events with Rachel Parrott cleaning up all age club records.

Walking reports by Carl Lawton

We got off to a flying start with new member Tony Pamah winning the 400m in style and Mark backing up well in the 'B' with 2nd place.

Dave Armstrong's blocks slipped in the 100, Phil Lovell fell foul of an over zealous judge and the weather in the pole vault and failed his opening height, and John Aska despite a dash by taxi just missed the hammer.

Apart from the disasters this meeting was one of the best that we have been involved in to date - the competition was fierce, especially the 400 and 400 relay with John Gladwin running 49.1 and finishing 5th. In the 400 relay we recorded one of our best times for years and finished last. Our other wins came from Gary (800m), Stu (1500), John (5000 B), Derek and Aham (Triple), Ken (discus and shot) also worth recording was Vince Cornibert, who threw a marvellous 60 metres in the Javelin and Phillip Goedluck who ran a great 200m and short relay. Andrew Rodney, Dave Armstrong, Phillip Goedluck, Tony Pamah, Derek Brown and Snowy Brooks (15 years since his debut in the British League) all made their first appearance.

items.summary: British Athletics League match 3 at Windsor, which Belgrave won with 273 points in probably their best ever team performance, assuring promotion to Division 3; with full results.
items.text:
8th July 1984 WINDSOR GRE/BAL MATCH 3

After Enfield we were in 3rd spot in the League and if we stayed there then we would be in Division three in 1985. At Windsor we aimed to consolidate this position.

As it turned out this was probably the greatest team ever fielded by Belgrave and the best result in any T & F Match in our long history.

Colin Gaynor returned to strengthen our sprints despite having problems with his hamstring. This made an enormous difference to our sprints. The remainder of the team were superb. It is worth reading the results in detail.

Andrew Rodney, Phillip Goedluck won the 'B' sprints in style - Jeremy Levine gave a boost to the high jump - Vince won the javelin, beating in style those who had been in front of him all season.

Jeremy Levine, Steve Smullen and Henry Cooper all made their British League debut.

Promotion to Div.3 was assured as a result of this victory, and there remained an outside chance of victory.

items.heading: 18th AUGUST 1984 BATTERSEA PARK GRE/BAL MATCH 4
items.summary: British Athletics League match 4, a Belgrave home promotion at Battersea Park, where a weakened team recorded a record 15 event wins but finished second to Windsor; with full results.
items.text:
18th AUGUST 1984 BATTERSEA PARK GRE/BAL MATCH 4

After our great win at Windsor, the last round match was a Belgrave home promotion at Battersea and what a great day it was - Geoff Davis did an amazing job - we had more officials than in the Coliseum, L.A. The GLC also did us proud with Battersea looking in great shape.

Our Team was in great shape too, but with the Nike Classic claiming Stu Paton, John Gladwin and Ernest Obeng and holidays accounting for Ken Onuaguluchi and Vince Cornibert, plus Paul Richley off to the U.S. we were just a bit short of our top men.

Nevertheless we recorded 15 wins, our highest ever, but we were pipped by Windsor on the day. Mark Sinclair chased Gary in the 1500 and both recorded good times - Mark ran a P.B. just missing sub 3.50. John Bicourt won the S/C in 9:05.5 a brilliant run for a 38 year old youngster! Neil Phillips won the 'B' discus as did Snowy in the 'B' shot. A great day with the Bels. still on the up - Div. 3 next year!

Thanks to all athletes, officials, recorders, groundsmen and helpers for a meeting that was typically Belgrave - just perfect.

Neil Phillips made his debut in the BAL team.

Note: Aham beat Derrick in the triple jump by 1cm! to make it 3:1 for the series.

items.heading: SOUTHERN LEAGUE ROUNDUP
items.summary: Review of Belgrave's 1984 Southern League season, in which the team won every match to gain promotion straight back to Division 2.
items.text:
SOUTHERN LEAGUE ROUNDUP

After the disappointing 1983 season when the 'B' team slipped to Division 3 in the Southern League, the Bels came roaring back in 1984 to win every single match and have bounced straight into Division 2. Not only did every match result in victory but the points scores were phenomenal - our highest being a massive 160 out of a possible 180 (which would need a win in every event, 'A' and 'B'). Our average score over the season was as high as we have ever attained in any single Southern League match over the past 15 years.

Why the change in our Fortunes? The reason surely is our increasing depth of good performers in virtually all events, and here we must thank Eddie Bojtler for pushing so many athletes in our direction. Now that our 4th, 5th and 6th ranked men can produce 40 metre hammer throws, run sub-23 200 metres etc., it means that even with athletes barred through 'A' team duty in the National League side, or on holiday or injured, we can still turn out an impressive 'B' side.

Now it's time to think of 1985. Can we go straight through Division 2 to the Southern League's premier competition? Its possible. And with members now having to prove themselves to get an outing with our 'B' side, perhaps we should start thinking seriously about a 'C' team - if we can find the officials to get it going!

SCAAA CHAMPIONSHIPS - C/PALACE - 1/2 JUNE - STUART PATON - 800M CHAMPION

There was an excellent turn out for this year's 'Southern' and plenty of good performances with Stuart Paton topping the bill by taking his first Southern Championship in his 'second' event - the 800m. Stuart always looked the danger man in what was a slow race early on as he covered every move of the leader. As they entered the final straight Stu' quickly opened a gap on the rest and comfortably held it to the line for an impressive win.

In the field, there were fine silver medals for Phil Lovell, who duplicated his performance of last year, and Ken Onuaguluchi, whose Discus series included 53.80 for a further improvement in our club record. Other pb's came from Mike Hayes- who made virtually all the running to win the 'standards' steeplechase (why he didn't meet the championship 'cut off' is something of a mystery) and from Aham Amadi in the Triple Jump.

HFC OLYMPIC TRIALS - C/PALACE - 6 JUNE:- Qualifying conditions were certainly tough for our two men-John Gladwin and Phil Lovell-but rightly so with Olympic places at stake. John faced an 800m final 2 1/4 hours after running 1.47.46 in the heats to qualify as a fastest loser- and that after a recent bout of illness. Sadly, he had little left to offer for the final and finished 8th in 1.49.46. Meanwhile,Phil faced an opening height of 4.80 in the vault- only 10cm below his best of last year. He gave it three good shots but made his exit.

AAA CHAMPIONSHIPS - C/PALACE - 23/24 JUNE - STUART PATON TAKES 1500M RECORD DOWN A NOTCH

100m- Ernest Obeng had been running into form with 10.47/21.25 for Loughbro' v AAA on 17 June and 10.55 to win an invitation meet in Belfast two days later, but he was below par here and didn't make the final. 11.07ht, 10.80sf.
800m- John Gladwin's heat time of 1.47.51 saw him through to the final as a fastest loser. The next day, John seemed without confidence at the start and he brought up the rear until the final straight when he found a way past Brown and Billy on the inside - but the medals were beyond recall. (1 Cram 1.46.84 6 J Gladwin 1.47.47.)
1500m- In the public eye, this event was notable for Elliott's defeat of the eventual Olympic Champion but for Belgrave supporters, attention was focused on Stuart Paton's attempt to make up for his disappointment of last year when not fully fit. With only 2 to go through from each heat by right, making the final was tough enough but Stu' was well placed throughout and produced the fastest finish to snatch first place on the line from Williamson - it may only have been a heat but nobody was sparing themselves at the end. The time - a new club record of 3.42.69. Of course it all had to be done again the next day and Stu' couldn't get up to the sharp end of a very tactical race. Nevertheless he recorded another 3.42 - and no doubt gained a lot from the experience. ( 1 Elliott 3.39.66 2 Coe 3.39.79 10 S Paton 3.42.98.)
Pole Vault- Phil Lovell seemed stuck on 4.60 upto this stage of the season and that was again the height he achieved here in 7th place. Nevertheless a fine placing in a national championship.
Discus- Ken Onuaguluchi was seen lofting out his warm up throws a long way but he couldn't catch a really big one in the competition. His best was a solid 52.58 and put him also in 7th place.

---------------------

Paul Richley made a long trip up to Stretford worthwhile on 26 June by running an excellent 3.48.7 in a BMC 1500m while Gary Staines took his 800m pb down to 1.50.0 in a BMC race at West London on 4 July.

INTER COUNTIES CHAMPIONSHIPS - BIRMINGHAM - 1 JULY - THREE CHAMPIONS

More Belgravians than ever before found their way to these championships as County selections. Titles were taken by Ernie Obeng(Sy)100m in 10.25w, a CBP and Ernie's 5th win in 7 years - a magnificent record; by Gary Staines(Herts)- the Mile in 4.09.53 - and Phil Lovell, finding some improved form (4.75) in the Pole Vault. Good points were also earned by Tony Pamah(Kent) 4th in the 400mh in 55.4 and Ken Onuaguluchi(Sy) 2nd in the Discus with 52.16. After a 4.11.15 heat in the mile, Stu' Paton dropped to 4.16.90 in the final for 9th place.

LAURISTON MILE - BATTERSEA PARK - 4 JULY:- This annual event saw three Bels way ahead of the field. Mark Sinclair took the lead straight away aiming for a fast run and John Warren made every use of the pace on Mark's shoulder. John had to let Mark go just before the bell as Mark kicked on to win in a useful 4.13.6 but John was rewarded with a pb of 4.18.7 in 2nd. Dave North completed the trio with 4.21.4.

ENGLAND v SPAIN v SWEDEN - GATESHEAD 6 JULY - JOHN (AND GARY) TAKE STUART'S RECORD

John Gladwin won further International selection for England over 1500m in this match and Gary Staines received a late invitation to run as a guest following his Inter-Counties win. So there was special interest as these two clashed for the first time. As usual, Gary got stuck in with the leaders straight away with John tucked in behind. In the final sprint, John squeezed past Gary but four others were just ahead in a blanket finish. Both men dipped under Stu's recent mark and the middle distance record spree was truly underway.(1 Theriot 3.41.28 2 Hutchings 3.41.33 5 J Gladwin 3.41.45 6 G Staines 3.41.76).Ernie Obeng ran as a guest in the 100m placing 2nd to McFarlane in 10.5.

PEUGEOT/TALBOT GAMES - C/PALACE - 13 JULY - 1000m RECORD:- John Gladwin took our club record for 1000m down to 2.19.14 although not helped by some uneven pacemaking, while Stu' Paton was also inside the previous best - which he held - with 2.21.37. Ernie Obeng was ahead of a former World record holder (Williams) and a former Olympic champion (Crawford) as he took 3rd place in the 100m in 10.69.

EDINBURGH GAMES - MEADOWBANK - 17 JULY - JOHN GOES UNDER 3.40 WITH STUART JUST BEHIND

Four days after their meeting in London, John and Stuart were brought together again for an invitation 1500m on Stu's 'home' track and both men again earned pb's - a couple of classy times (shown at the top of the All Time list) and forward placings in a large field behind the World Record holder who won in 3.36.90. Both men finished well and will go faster when hanging on further up the front of one of these pace made races. Ernest Obeng was 3rd behind Wells and Krulee in the 100m in 10.46.

items.heading: GARY EQUALS 1 MILE RECORD WHILE JOHN GOES ROUND THE WORLD
items.summary: Notes on Gary Staines equalling the club mile record at West London Stadium and running well in a gale at Jarrow, and John Gladwin winning an international 1500m in Taipei.
items.text:
GARY EQUALS 1 MILE RECORD WHILE JOHN GOES ROUND THE WORLD

GARY STAINES equalled the club mile record at West London Stadium on 5 September when winning the Open Graded 'A' race in 4.02.1 on one of the first cold evenings of the late Summer. But those weather conditions were nothing compared to the gale force winds he had to contend with four days later at a meeting to open the new Jarrow track. That Gary should run 4.03.67 was therefore an exceptional effort. Cram and Walker were less than 6, and 5, seconds ahead, respectively and if you reckon on them being worth 3.49/3.50 normally , it shows the true merit of Gary's run.

------------

Members of this club have competed in many parts of the World but new ground must have been broken by John Gladwin when he won an International 1500m in Taipei in September in 3.52.25 and took second place in the 800 in 1.48.92. So if you get offered a job lot of training shoes - made in Taiwan - you'll know where they came from!

items.heading: ERNEST OBENG'S LATE SEASON UPS AND DOWNS
items.summary: Account of Ernest Obeng's 1984 season, including his expulsion from the Los Angeles Olympics by Ghanaian officials and his late-season return to form, with a photograph from the Peugeot Games.
items.text:
ERNEST OBENG'S LATE SEASON UPS AND DOWNS

1984 was a year of mixed fortune for our leading sprinter. He struggled to find his best form early on but it was Olympic year and, having missed out on Moscow, Ernie was encouraged enough to pay his own way to LA for probably his last chance to compete in the great event. Well no doubt you know the story of Ernie's expulsion from the Games by Ghanaian officials in what seems an incredible case of victimisation. It was obviously a great disappointment to him not to be able to compete and the character assassination that went with the affair added insult to injury.

It was perhaps some small consolation to Ernie that he should hit some of his best ever form in August - as if to show that he would have performed with great credit to his country in LA. For following a couple of ordinary clockings at the Nike Classic and in Budapest when still coping with jet lag, he flew to a 10.25 timing (his 3rd fastest legal mark) in Zurich on 22 August, only headed by Olympic Bronze Medallist Ben Johnson and Osvaldo Lara - winner of the Eastern Block 'Friendship' Games. Then in Rieti,Italy on 2 September he recorded 10.32 (+0.7) behind Penalver and Lara.

At the IAC/Coca-Cola meeting on 7 September, Ernie gave us at home the first glimpse of this return to form. He snapped away from the blocks to win his heat easing up in 10.45 into a slight headwind - but what a pity the start of the final was such a shambles with McFarlane getting a clear flyer and the race not being recalled by the starter. Although Lara's pick-up enabled him to win, Ernie,at a disadvantage with his own fast start pre-empted, couldn't quite make up the deficit and he finished 3rd in 10.38.

Ernest Obeng's Belgrave Honours badge well to the fore in the Peugeot Games held at the Crystal Palace on July 13th, - probably the last occasion he will wear Ghana's colours as he has vowed not to compete again for the Country which treated him so shabbily in Los Angeles Olympics. Wells won in 10.46. Press Association Photo.

items.text:
Nike Blackheath H~ 25 x 1mile

29th SEPTEMBER 1984 CRYSTAL PALACE NIKE 25x1 MILE RELAY

Last year's first ever win in this Nationwide event led us to hope that with a better team (on paper) we could repeat our success. Sale running at Manchester had other ideas and as our 'A' team turned in times just marginally slower than we had anticipated Sale improved on their efforts of last year. We ran as usual at the Crystal Palace venue while 80 or so teams competed at 8 other venues. The race was close right up to the 18 mile mark when Pat Chester running for TVH ran a 4.08 effort to snatch the lead from the Bels. Nigel Clarke got a bit carried away on the next leg as the excitement built and ran his first 400 in 57.7! It was left to Peter Gilbey to take us into a lead which increased to 3 minutes over TVH over the next 5 miles. Everyone had been blaming the cold windy conditions for the 'slow' times, but either they were wrong or Gary Staines' 4.06 on the last leg was really something special. Running at even pace Gary finished in great style and even had to contend with being baulked by 2 Croydon runners who ran right in front of him as they changed the baton at the 2 lap mark. Several of our 'A' team men had just returned from holidays and it showed in their times. Our youngsters though ran superbly with Youths John Booth and Glyn Tiernan performing well as did Junior Richard O'Hara who is beginning to look a class runner.

In the 'B' team Francis Ward, who has returned from 2 years in the U.S.A. proved fastest with Andy Moore close behind. Our 'D' team comprised young members having an average age of 13 years and their general high level of performance promises well for the future.

Our thanks to Bill Couzens, Brian Pritchard and Derek Jones plus their families who put up with the trying conditions while organising and recording through the morning and afternoon sessions. Jim and Dave Mote organised the Young Athletes and yours truly the 'A'.

Bill Laws

items.heading: GARY STAINES' EXTRAORDINARY WEEK.
items.summary: Note on Gary Staines' week in July 1984 in which he ran five top races, including winning the Inter-Counties mile and racing for England at Gateshead.
items.text:
GARY STAINES' EXTRAORDINARY WEEK.

Team spirit has been a particular part of our continueing upward path in the British Athletics League. Perhaps the most remarkable example was the case of Gary Staines who in one hectic week in July ran 5 top class races. On the Sunday he ran a heat and won the final of the Inter-Counties 1 mile. On the Wednesday in an Open Meeting he ran a p.b. 800m in 1.50.0. On the Friday he worked in the morning and then dashed up to Gateshead to guest in the England v Spain v Sweden International where he ducked under Stuart's 1500m Club record and was prominant on Television as he led for 3 laps . And on the Saturday he travelled with the BAL team to Windsor and won the 800m as we achieved a massive points win over our rivals.
With support like that our Officials know that all the hard work behind the scenes is worthwhile!

people.name: Gary Staines
people.note: won Inter-Counties 1 mile; 800m p.b. 1.50.0; broke club 1500m record in England v Spain v Sweden at Gateshead; won BAL 800m at Windsor

items.heading: OLIVER GOES SECOND ON ALL TIME LIST
items.summary: Report and full results of the Yacht 3 handicap at Wimbledon on 6 October 1984, won from scratch by Oliver Foote with the 4th fastest time ever on the course behind Gerry North's three.
items.text:
OLIVER GOES SECOND ON ALL TIME LIST

6th OCTOBER 1984 WIMBLEDON YACHT 3 HANDICAP

It is very seldom that the speedy scratch markers take the handicapper to the cleaners in this event. Generally a few of our slower runners manage to leg it off an over-generous mark. This year it was different due to some exceptionally fine runs from our faster men. Chris Millbank showed what progress a year's training can provide as he knocked a remarkable 2½ minutes off last years debut time. First year Junior, Richard O'Hara translated his recent track form to a fine first run round this course as too did Marcello Bizio. Leo Lyons showed a return to form after prolonged injury while 15 year old Gary McGurren ran an exceptional 16.16 in his first attempt at this event. But pride of place must go to Oliver Foote who took the field apart as he moved from scratch through to take the lead at Wimbledon Village after which he coasted to a 9 sec. lead. His time of 14.34 was the 4th fastest ever round this traditional Club course, the first three all being recorded by Gerry North (14.15, 14.21, and 14.21). Gerry's 14.15 clocking was in 1962 - the year he won the English Senior National Cross Country Champs. As Steve Williams remarked - "This was Oliver's finest win to date".

Several ladies competed in this years race, fastest of whom was new member Jill Davies.

B = Boy, Y = Youth, J = Junior, L = Lady

SURREY CROSS COUNTRY LEAGUE - DIVISION 1

13th OCTOBER 1984 WIMBLEDON SURREY C.C. LEAGUE - DIV.I

A marginally better performance than last year's opening disaster. Gary Staines cut his foot and was forced to retire while Oliver Foote fell over and did well to get up to 8th place. items.heading: FIRST RELAY SUCCESS AS BELGRAVE WIN INAUGURAL LONDON RELAY
items.summary: Report and results of Belgrave's win in the inaugural 'Zatopek' 6 x 4½km Thames Relay in the City of London on 21 October 1984, organised by Ron Clarke and Dave Bedford, with a photo of anchor John Gladwin.
items.text:
FIRST RELAY SUCCESS AS BELGRAVE WIN INAUGURAL LONDON RELAY

21st OCTOBER 1984 CITY OF LONDON 'ZATOPEK' 6x4½km THAMES RELAY

This inaugural race organised by ex 10,000m world record holders Ron Clarke and Dave Bedford was well publicised in the Local and National press and despite the previous day's National 6 stage relay received a great response from athletes and spectators. The course, chosen to keep clear of traffic, was not up to Championship Standards involving as it did several flights of steps. Nevertheless the atmosphere was there with commentary by Capital Radio's Kelly Temple and this coupled with free lunch and a drink plus party made the day memorable particularly for the loyal lady supporters. But to the race.

This was the first time we had got our strongest 6 together. Not all were fully fit and with many still beginning a gradual build up we weren't certain if the established relay stars would prove too strong for us. The start saw 60 runners streaming over Southwark Bridge with Oliver Foote tucked in in about 12th place. As the fast pace began to bite a group of 3 broke away and at the first change over Oliver was only 3 seconds down on Enfield's leader Keith Doulton. Dave North took it steadily moving into second spot as a gap of around 8 seconds opened between him and the leader. Looking more relaxed than usual and picking up the pace our man gradually pulled back the difference to hand over to Gary Staines in the lead. Gary moved off fast opened up a gap of 15 seconds, relaxed and then had a fright as Andy Catton of Ilford stormed past at the 2 mile mark. Not to be put off Gary knuckled down to some hard work and needed his sprint finish to put us back in the lead. Stuart Paton looked to be moving well as he opened the gap to around 25 seconds which Mark Sinclair needed as Kevin Steer of Ilford took off after him on the 5th leg. The race bubbled at this point as Kevin gradually reduced the gap to get within 3 seconds of Mark 600m out. It was at this point that Mark kicked and the Ilford mans efforts had been in vain. John Gladwin took off as though he was in a fast 1500 and broke Ilfords last stage runner to such an extent that they drifted back to 4th as Keith Palmer ran the fastest leg of the day to bring Highgate into second place 50 seconds adrift. Our'B' team men put up some good times to make a great day for Belgrave.

items.text:
VETS. CORNER

There were varying fortunes for our Vets on the track and road. With the European Vets T & F Championships being held in Brighton this year we could have expected some medal successes, but it was not to be. Laurie O'Hara who earlier in the year had established a U.K. over 50's 1500m record with 4:13.9 only managed 4th at Brighton as he recorded 4:15.1 just 0.1 sec. off the bronze in a close finish. If he had opted for the 5000m there would have been gold but with an entry fee of £5 plus £5 per event it didn't encourage doubling up. Snowy Brooker also travelled hopefully to Brighton, having put in some excellent performances in our British League team but despite some first class marks in the early events he managed 3 'no-throws' in the discus and was eliminated.

Laurie later went on to win the Southern 10 Miles Vets Champs. with a remarkable 53.36 as he led our Vets to a team Silver.

items.heading: DUNLOP YOUNG ATHLETES LEAGUE
items.summary: Report on Belgrave's four 1984 Dunlop Young Athletes League matches (Battersea Park, Guildford, Redhill, Portsmouth), with outstanding performances, match results and final league positions (Belgrave third).
items.text:
YOUNG ATHLETES

DUNLOP YOUNG ATHLETES LEAGUE

This years league competition has been an up and down affair, with successes being sandwiched between disappointments.

The following are short reports covering our four matches, highlighting the outstanding performances from these meetings.

6th MAY 1984 BATTERSEA PARK MATCH 1

As our first meeting dawned we found ourselves in disarray after the long winter break. Our weaknesses were startingly apparent in the technical field events where absences let down our extremely strong track team. At the end of the day we scored 17 wins, 16 seconds, 4 thirds and 17 other places, leaving 18 events not covered. The failure to cover these events caused our immediate loss of a minimum of 18 points.

Outstanding performances -

P.Goedluck Y.200 (23.3) & 100 (11.5); G.Warr Y(B) 200 (24.7) & 100 (11.9) R.Iles C(A) 1500 (5.08.7); D.Ward B(A) 1500 (4.42.1); D.Steward B(B) 1500 (4.35.2); S.Richards Y(A) 400 (54.8); D.Ashford B(A) 3000 (10.28.1); J.Caines B(B) 3000 (11.24); B.Zreik B(B) HJ:(1.50) & B(A) 800 (2:17.5); A.Ross C(A) 800 (2:25.3); C.Gardener Y(A) 100H (15.1). Youths 4x100 (46.2).

Results: 1.Sutton & Cheam 248; 2.Surrey Beagles 228; 3.Fareham 202 4.BELGRAVE 186; 5.Walton 147.

3rd JUNE 1984 GUILDFORD MATCH 2

A warm but blustery day greeted us at Guildford. Our team had been dramatically strengthened since the match at Battersea Park and particularly in the field we felt in a far better state to face the competition. The match was very close with several athletes doubling up to cover empty places in some events, and at the end of the day it was these commendable actions added to the other impressive individual results which gave us the day by ½ a point. On this occasion we notched up 18 wins, 15 seconds, 11 thirds and 20 other places leaving only 8 events empty.

Outstanding performances -

24th JUNE 1984 REDHILL MATCH 3

Redhill was the first meeting at which we fielded a team selected by the newly formed Young Athletes Committee.

The weather was warm and the athletics hot. With athletes now able to concentrate on their specialist events results were impressive with 23 wins, 19 seconds, 12 thirds and 12 other places. 6 events were still empty but this was understandable when one realises that 12 of the team were representing Surrey and London in the School's Triangular match and were therefore unable to compete for us.

Outstanding performances -

D.Ashford B(A) PV (1.75); D.McCarthy B(B) PB (1.30) & (B) JT (20.60); G.Warr Y(A) 200 (24.0) & (A) 100 (11.7); G.Pastana Y(B) 200 (24.5); D.Maloney B(B) 200 (27.0); I.Gilley C(A) 200 (27.7); A.Ross C(B) 200 (28.4) & (A) 100 (13.8); J.Mole Y(A) TJ (11.42); G.Tiernan Y(A) 1500 (4:35.7); G.Allison B(A) 80H (12.8) & (A) HJ (1.50); J.Beasty Y(A) 3000 (10.14.4); K.McDonagh Y(B) 3000 (10:15.4) & (B) 1500SC (5:34.7); D.Rose Y(B) 100H (18.6); S.Sbicca B(B) HJ (1.30); S.Beaumont Y(A) 800 (2.10.1).

Colts 4x100 (57.2) Youths 4x100 (50.2) & 4x400 (3:52.4).

These results gave us our second win, this time by a clear 24 points.

Results: 1.BELGRAVE 258; 2.Surrey Beagles 222; 3.Guildford 211; 4.Camberley 165; 5.Walton 121.

This moved us up into second place in the league behind Sutton & Cheam. All we needed was an average team performance in our last meeting and we would be guaranteed a place in the promotion qualifying meeting at our home track, Battersea Park.

As we left Redhill, hopes were high that we could join our senior teams in their promotion celebrations.

29th JULY 1984 PORTSMOUTH MATCH 4

Tomorrow never comes. Our team for Portsmouth, devastatingly depleted by unavoidable holidays and sickness, was just a poor shadow of the team at Redhill.

Our athletes pushed themselves to the maximum, almost all competing in their statutory 4 events. Team morale remained high though unfortunately morale alone doesn't win meetings and with no competitors in 23 out of 72 events a poor result was unavoidable. However all credit must go to the athletes and parents who attended on what was a beautiful day at an excellent facility.

Outstanding performances -

I.Gilley C(A) 200 (27.7); G.Warr Y(A) 200 (24.5) & (A) 100 (12.4); D.Sewell B(A) ST (12.06) & (A) JAV (76.58); G.Allison B(A) 80H (13.0) & (A) 800 (2.17.6); J.Mole Y(B) TJ (11.80).

This put Fareham into the qualifying match, beating us by one point and left Belgrave with the commitment to show their true match dominating colours in 1985.

items.heading: THAMESIDE LEAGUE
items.summary: Report on the 1984 Thameside League for boys and colts, expanded to include women's teams, with final positions and special mention of Gavin Warr and Gareth Allison.
items.text:
THAMESIDE LEAGUE

This Belgrave brainchild, created ostensibly to provide competition for boys up to 14 years of age, was successfully expanded this year to incorporate five women's teams, whose exploits are reported in the Women's Section. In addition to the inter-club events it includes numerous non-scoring competitions in a relaxed atmosphere, where boys can experiment with new events.

When reporting the results of our Boys and Colts in this competition it must be said that they appear disappointing because both teams finished near to the bottom of their leagues. This is because, in many cases, this year the emphasis has been to provide club competition for those boys who only occasionally have the opportunity to take part in the Young Athletes League, while at the same time providing a series of non-scoring races for others.

Both these objectives were achieved, but at the expense of the league position. It was gratifying also to see the popularity of this venture grow with each meeting with the numbers of competitors in June and July, before the holidays began to thin the ranks, threatening to swamp the organisers. All in all it has been a happy and (with the aforementioned qualification) successful season.

With all competing clubs already booking their places for next year we look forward to even greater achievements.

Our congratulations go to Croydon Harriers Boys and Camberley A.C. Colts, but warn them, we shall be after the trophies next year.

The individual performances are too numerous to mention in this report, but the final league tables were as follows

THAMESIDE LEAGUE - FINAL POSITIONS.

COLTS; 1. Camberley 22pts., 2. Croydon 18pts., 3. Twick.& Ran. 15pts., 4. HHH 14pts., 5. BELGRAVE 8pts., 6. Queens Park H 7pts.

BOYS; 1. Croydon 22pts., 2. HHH 21pts., 3. Camberley 17pts., 4. BELGRAVE 10pts., 5. Queens Pk 8pts., 6. Twick.& Ran. 6pts.

In summing up the season special mention must be made of the exploits of Gavin Warr (Youth) and Gareth Allison (Boy). Gavin competed in every Young Athletes League and won every race in which he competed. Gareth competed in both Young Athletes and Thameside Leagues and proved to be the club's only high-jumping middle-distance hurdler.

Finally the Young Athletes sub committee wish to thank all the parents and officials who supported us so consistently throughout the season.

Reports by Jim & Dave Mote.

items.heading: WITH THE LADIES
items.summary: Ladies Secretary Derek Jones's review of the women's 1984 season: 7th in the Womens Southern League, Midweek League win, county vests and medals, individual progress, and thanks to helpers.
items.text:
WITH THE LADIES

It has been quite an exciting season, with us finishing in 7th position in the Womens Southern League. This was our best position since 1980. In this League after 4 3rd placings we were lying 12th and we won the last 2. The last meeting was against strong opposition and we beat Aldershot, a team we had never beaten before so that was really pleasing. The Thameside League was a good replacement for the Lily B League and we hope that this will be continued for next season, especially as the athletes seemed to enjoy the competition. After a period of 6 years we re-entered the Midweek League (very similar in content to the Rosenheim League) and as we won every match we won the League very convincingly. There were plenty of places for the Non-scorers and everyone who came along was able to get competition.

Our Junior relay team was unbeaten in all 6 Southern League, all 4 Thameside League and all 6 Midweek League races which is another good record. During the Season Club records were broken on at least 40 occasions.

Three of our athletes gained their county vests. Wendy Dunsford represented Middlesex in a meeting in May held at Motspur Park, whilst Veronica St. Ange competed for Surrey in a representative match in July at Copthall and Rosemary Honeychurch represented Surrey in the Southern Womens Inter Counties Championships in August held at Crystal Palace.

Three of our athletes also won Gold in County Championships. Rosemary Honeychurch won the 3000m in the Surrey Championships, whilst Cindy James and Angela Abrams won the 100m and Hurdles in the Middlesex Championships. Our total tally of medals in both County Championships was 12, with 6 Silvers and 3 Bronzes. So congratulations to all the medal winners and all those who took part. This was our best haul of medals in County Championships as well.

Our walkers were well represented in the English Schools Walking Championships with London being represented by Gail Porter, Kim Marsh, Isobel Young and Charlotte Chirstou and Surrey and Essex being represented by Rachael Parrott and Joanne McGroder respectively.

Picking out individuals it is worth noting that Jessica Palmer has continued the improvement she showed from last season and was joined in the Sprints by Yvette Edward Cindy James, Angela Abrams and Andrea Abrams, Nina Christou and Tracy Ritson. Angela Abrams and Nina Christou, both improved their Hurdles technique and had good backing from Cindy James. Cindy proved to be a good all-round athlete with improvements to her Shot and Discus. We were a bit short of junior middle distance runners, but those who did the events tried their best but the improvement shown by Jackie Stone was very encouraging as well as winning Silver in the Surrey Championships. Angela Abrams and her twin sister Andrea improved their marks in the Long Jump and Andrea began to do better in the high jump but must learn to concentrate harder. The record book has been re-written by Rachael Parrott in the walks and now holds all the Girls records as well as improving upon the Girls Javelin record.

In the Seniors the middle distance team of Rosemary Honeychurch who has knocked over a minute off her 3000m record this season and there is probably more to come, Vicky Mitchell, Gail Porter ably backed by Davina Cameron and Georgina Tura did well. The Sprinters did not do as well as the Middle Distance runners but Andrea Coore, Shirley Daure, Penny Garnons-Williams well backed by Dezrine Conard, Adele Peck, and when they were able to come to meetings Erica Goldson and Susan Wilkinson

Our Throwing team of Wendy Dunsford, Debbie Roberts, Veronica St. Ange as well as Perrican Bayar when she was available proved almost unbeatable. They won through although not always at their best and Veronica competed with broken bones in her foot. It is perhaps worth noting that we have competed in 40 Southern League fixtures since 1977 and Wendy has only missed 2 of them. She has been ever-present since June 1979 and in the Shot in the 30 matches since we were promoted to Division 3 has scored 139 points out of a possible 150.

Our Walkers have kept Belgrave vests to the fore and these have been led very well by Rachael Parrott ably backed by Isobel Young, Charlotte Christou and were ably backed by Kelly Owen, Julie Field and Teresa Thirlwall.

For all these results thanks must go to a great number of people who have helped me no end this season. Among those who should be mentioned are Ted Weldin, Dave Wenham, and Graham Thom for their help in the Hurdles, Jumps and Sprints. Also for his efforts in the Walks, thanks must go to Dave Sharpe, who has turned up at Battersea Park from Dagenham despite having a number of problems during the summer. Thanks to Derek Crookes too for also helping with the Middle Distance girls during the back end of the season. Last, but not least my thanks must go to Harry Porter and Frank Simmons for the work they do and their help and advice during the Season. Thanks to all the parents who come along and help and support and have made friends with each other and thanks to Sue Parrott for taking over the Press Representative's job. It is very pleasant to have so many people eager and willing to help and to those who come along to help judge at meetings as well. We could have done with a few more of these. After all we are here to help and encourage athletes and athletics and this cannot be done by not supporting BELGRAVE. We need help especially at Home Matches and even recording helps as Wyn Sheppard who was at all our home matches doing just that, or serving teas. Every little helps, so why not come and enjoy a day out seeing youngsters enjoy themselves.

If I have missed anybody in my thanks during the season, then the omission was not really intentional. Thanks to all who have helped and encouraged or brought their children along to meetings by car.

DEREK JONES
Ladies Secretary

items.text:
1st SEPTEMBER 1984 DARTFORD SOUTHERN LEAGUE DIV.3 (S)

Results: 1.BELGRAVE 178; 2.Ald.Farn.& Dist. 176½; 3.Dartford H.148; 4.Basingstoke A.C. 145½; 5.Fleet & Crookham A.C. 37.

This was a really splendid result for us as two of the teams we beat were in 5th and 6th position in the Division. This also was the first time that we have beaten Aldershot so that result was even more pleasing.

This result meant that we finished in 7th position in the Division which is the best that we have done since 1980. It also means that we finish well above Hercules Wimbledon and with the last result just pushed Kingston back into 8th place.
